A consensus four-star recruit and former [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]] commit, Lecque chose to forgo [[college basketball]] and immediately entered the [[2019 NBA draft]]. ==Early life== Lecque was born in [[Manhattan|Manhattan, New York]] and lived in [[The Bronx]] until he was three years old. Both of his parents worked in [[Harlem]], his father at a barbershop and his mother at a hospital. As a toddler, Lecque moved with his family to [[Teaneck, New Jersey]], where he attended [[primary school|elementary]] and [[middle school]].{{cite web |last1=Jones |first1=Ryan |title=Jalen Lecque Is Representing New York City to the Fullest |url=https://www.slamonline.com/the-magazine/jalen-lecque-feature/ |website=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]] |accessdate=May 14, 2019 |date=August 15, 2018}} ==High school career== Instead of attending his local school [[Teaneck High School]], Lecque decided to enroll at [[Monsignor Scanlan High School]] in The Bronx because of its superior basketball program.{{cite web |last1=Cordova |first1=David |title=Rook Season: Jalen Lecque Goes From Underrated Player in CHSAA to High-Major Recruit |url=https://davesjoint.net/2017/06/15/rook-season-jalen-lecque-goes-from-underrated-player-in-chsaa-to-high-major-recruit/ |publisher=Dave's Joint |accessdate=May 14, 2019 |date=June 15, 2017}} In the 2016–17 season, he averaged about 11 points per game.{{cite web |last1=Richey |first1=Scott |title=Illinois offers 2019 point guard |url=http://www.news-gazette.com/sports/illini-sports/mens-basketball/2017-07-15/illinois-offers-2019-point-guard.html |website=[[The News-Gazette (Champaign–Urbana)|The News-Gazette]] |accessdate=May 14, 2019 |date=July 15, 2017}} In April 2017, Lecque saw breakout success with Southern Stampede at the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] (EYBL), helping him gain interest from many prominent [[NCAA Division I]] programs.{{cite web |last1=Zagoria |first1=Adam |title=Bronx Native Jalen Lecque Becoming Breakout Star on EYBL Circuit |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2017/04/29/bronx-native-jalen-lecque-becoming-breakout-star-eybl-circuit/ |publisher=ZagsBlog |accessdate=May 14, 2019 |date=April 29, 2017}} Entering the 2017–18 season, Lecque transferred to [[Christ School (North Carolina)|Christ School]] in [[Arden, North Carolina]] while [[reclassification (education)|reclassifying]] from the 2018 to 2019 class.{{cite web |last1=Lawless |first1=Pat |title=Kentucky, Texas, Oregon, Maryland and more are prioritizing Jalen Lecque - 2019 guard breaks down his recruitment |url=https://www.madehoops.com/news_article/show/865068 |publisher=Made Hoops |accessdate=May 14, 2019 |date=December 9, 2017 }}{{Dead link|date=September 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}{{cite web |last1=Lane |first1=Chris |title=2019 guard Jalen Lecque taking unofficial visit to Villanova |url=https://www.vuhoops.com/2017/6/15/15809196/villanova-basketball-recruiting-2019-guard-jalen-lecque-unofficial-visit |publisher=VU Hoops |accessdate=May 14, 2019 |date=June 15, 2017}} He was drawn to the school for not only basketball, but also academics. Lecque averaged 20.1 points, 9.1 rebounds, and 9.3 assists per game, leading his team to the 3A North Carolina Independent School Athletic Association (NCISAA) state semifinals. He was named ''[[Asheville Citizen-Times]]'' All-[[Western North Carolina]] (WNC) Player of the Year and earned NCISAA All-State honors.{{cite web |last1=Thompson |first1=David |title=All-WNC Boys Basketball Team |url=https://www.citizen-times.com/story/sports/high-school/hshuddle/2018/03/20/all-wnc-boys-basketball-team/441902002/ |website=[[Asheville Citizen-Times]] |accessdate=May 14, 2019 |date=March 20, 2018}} On July 30, 2018, Lecque announced that he would transfer to [[Brewster Academy]] in [[Wolfeboro, New Hampshire]] for his senior season.{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=Five-star SG Jalen Lecque to transfer to Brewster Academy |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/five-star-sg-jalen-lecque-to-transfer-to-brewster-academy |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=May 14, 2019 |date=July 30, 2018}} On April 20, 2019, Lecque declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]].{{cite web |last1=Abdeldaiem |first1=Alaa |title=NC State Commit Jalen Lecque Declares for 2019 NBA Draft |url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2019/04/20/jalen-lecque-nc-state-commit-declares-draft |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |accessdate=May 14, 2019 |date=April 20, 2019}} On May 29, 2019, he remained in the NBA draft past the withdrawal deadline, ensuring that he would not play at the college level.{{cite web |last1=Hines |first1=Travis |title=NC State recruit Jalen Lecque staying in draft |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2019/05/29/nc-state-recruit-jalen-lecque-staying-in-draft/ |publisher=[[NBC Sports]] |accessdate=May 29, 2019 |date=May 29, 2019}} On May 8, 2019, Lecque was named one of 77 total players participating in the [[NBA Draft Combine]] later in the month.{{cite web |title=Sixty-six players expected to attend NBA Draft Combine |url=https://www.nba.com/article/2019/05/08/66-players-attend-nba-draft-combine |publisher=[[National Basketball Association]] |accessdate=May 23, 2019 |date=May 8, 2019}} He recorded a 43-inch maximum [[vertical jump|vertical leap]], the highest at the combine, and left the combine early after receiving positive feedback from NBA teams.{{cite web |last1=Krest |first1=Shawn |title=Little, Lecque among winners at NBA Draft Combine |url=https://nsjonline.com/article/2019/05/little-lecque-among-winners-at-nba-draft-combine/ |website=[[North State Journal]] |accessdate=May 23, 2019 ==Professional career== ===Phoenix Suns (2019–2020)=== Lecque committed to play college basketball for the [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|North Carolina State Wolfpack]] as a freshman for the 2019–2020 season, but instead, because of his eligibility and age decided to abstain from a collegiate career and rescind his commitment.{{Cite web|title=Jalen Lecque to Forgo Playing at NC State, Enter 2019 NBA Draft|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2776121-jalen-lecque-to-forgo-playing-at-nc-state-enter-2019-nba-draft|access-date=March 5, 2021|website=Bleacher Report|language=en}} Lecque was not drafted in the [[2019 NBA draft]] on June 20. He was signed to a 4-year deal, 2 years guaranteed, by the [[Phoenix Suns]] on July 6.{{cite web|title=Suns Sign Johnson, Jerome, Lecque|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-johnson-jerome-lecque|website=NBA.com|accessdate=July 9, 2019|date=July 6, 2019}} On October 28, Lecque was assigned to the [[Motor City Cruise|Northern Arizona Suns]] for the start of the [[2019–20 NBA G League season]].{{cite web|title=Jalen Lecque Assigned to Northern Arizona Suns|url=https://northernarizona.gleague.nba.com/news/jalen-lecque-assigned-to-northern-arizona-suns/|website=nba.com|accessdate=November 7, 2019|date=October 28, 2019|archive-date=November 11, Phoenix on multiple assignments throughout the season.{{cite web|title=Phoenix Recalls Jerome and Lecque From NAZ debut on January 16, playing in only two minutes for the Suns' 121–98 win over the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|title=Ayton shines as Suns pound Knicks 121-98|url=https://www.nba.com/games/20200116/PHXNYK#/boxscore|website=NBA.com|first=Jeffrey|last=Bernstein|date=January 16, 2020|accessdate=January 21, 2020}} ===Indiana Pacers (2020–2021)=== On November 16, 2020, Lecque was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] alongside [[Ty Jerome]], [[Ricky Rubio]], [[Kelly Oubre Jr.]], and a 2022 first-round pick in exchange for [[Chris Paul]] and [[Abdel Nader]].{{cite web |title=Thunder Acquires Ty Jerome, Jalen Lecque, Kelly Oubre Jr., Ricky Rubio and 2022 First-Round Draft Pick |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/acquisitions-201116 |website=NBA.com |accessdate=November 16, 2020 |date=November 16, 2020}} On November 25, 2020, Lecque was traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in exchange for [[T. J. Leaf]] and a future second-round pick.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-acquire-jalen-lecque-oklahoma-city|title=Pacers Acquire Jalen Lecque from Oklahoma City|work=NBA.com|date=November 25, 2020}} On March 25, 2021, Lecque was waived by the Pacers.{{cite web|title=Pacers Waive Lecque|date=March 25, 2021|website=NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-waive-lecque|access-date=March 26, 2021}} === Wisconsin Herd (2021–2022) === On October 15, 2021, Lecque signed a training camp deal with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|title= The Milwaukee Bucks have signed Jalen Lecque to a training camp deal |date=October 15, 2021|website=Twitter.com|url= https://twitter.com/KeithSmithNBA/status/1448963813743730706 |access-date=October 15, 2021}} He joined the [[Wisconsin Herd]] as an affiliate player.{{cite web |title=Wisconsin Herd Announces 2021 Training Camp Roster |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/wisconsin-herd-announces-2021-training-camp-roster/n-5758540 |website=Our Sports Central |access-date=October 31, 2021 named to the opening night roster for the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].{{cite web|title=Vipers Finalize 2022-23 Opening Night Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/vipers-finalize-2022-23-opening-night-roster/n-5895553|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 3, 2022|access-date=November 3, 2022}}
